contexts.text: The mark set on Cain = faith inviolable. AC 392.
Jehovah set a mark on Cain () = that the Lord distinguished faith in a singular manner. To put a mark on anyone = to distinguish. Illustrated. AE 427:6, Explained.
A sign is called a mark. Illustrated.
This is the sign of the covenant... () = no other sign than an indication of the presence of the Lord in charity. AC 1044. AC 1059.
Great signs and wonders () = confirmations and persuasions from external appearances and fallacies by which the simple suffer themselves to be seduced.
The sign of the Son of Man in heaven () = the appearing of truth Divine. It was this appearing, or sign, as to which the disciples asked: What shall be the sign of Thy coming? HH 1:2. DSS 14:2.
Such heaps were anciently for a mark, etc.
Baptism is a sign of regeneration, to remember it. HH 329.
The pillars erected were for a mark, etc.
No stops in the ancient Hebrew.
This shall be a sign to thee that I have sent thee () = the Knowledge that the Divine proceeded from Him. A sign = a confirmation of the Truth, and thence the Knowledge that it is so.
(Signification of Moses' three signs.) AC 6971. AC 6973.
(The spiritual) will not receive what Truth Divine says, unless they see that it is so; thus unless they see signs.
The three signs represent their state if they did not believe.
Wherewith thou shalt do signs () = the consequent illustration and confirmation of Truths. A sign = the confirmation of Truths. AC 7060.

I will multiply My signs and wonders () = admonitions of every kind, and that nothing should be wanting. Explained. Signs and wonders = confirmations of the Truth; also media of Divine power; here, admonitions.
Wonders and signs were done with such as were in external worship... Explained.

Tomorrow shall this sign be () = the manifestation of Divine power thence for ever... A sign = confirmation of the Truth, and thus Knowledge, consequently a manifestation of Divine power; for the Truth was formerly manifested by signs, and Divine power at the same time.

That I may put these My signs in the midst of him () = that the evil may know that they are in evil, and that the good may be illustrated concerning the state of those who live evilly within the Church. Explained.
Two signs which appear to these Spirits (of Jupiter) when they are with man. Described.
For a sign upon the houses () = a testification of the will of good. To be for a sign = a testification.
For a sign upon thy hand () = perpetually in the will. A sign = perpetual remembrance.
A memorial is predicated of the Intellectual; and a sign, of the Voluntary.
Under Nissi, see this reference.
The signs that sins are remitted. Enumerated.
The signs that sins are not remitted. Enumerated.
See Forehead.
A sign between Me and you () = that it is the principal thing by which they who are of the Church are known in Heaven. Explained. AC 10372.
On the signs and visitations before the Last Judgment. General article.
That no one is reformed by miracles and signs, because they compel. General article.
Good works (said to be) signs of faith.

A great sign seen in heaven () = revelation by the Lord concerning His New Church... A sign from Heaven, here, = a revelation about future things... A sign, in the Word, is said about future things, and then it is a revelation; and it is said about the Truth, and then it is a testification; and it is also said about the quality of the state and Thing, and then it is a manifestation. Illustrated. AE 706.
Another sign seen in heaven () = a revelation from the Lord concerning those who are against the New Church.
He does great signs () = testifications that the (falsities) they teach are true. Because formerly signs were done in order that the Truth might be testified. AR 704. AR 834.
That testifications that a thing is true are signified by signs. Illustrated.
The signs given him to do before the beast () = testifications and proofs.
Another sign in heaven, great and marvellous () = revelation about the state of the Church on earth, as to its love and faith. AE 926, Explained.
Without the Christian sign, which is baptism...
What are indications without signs (or marks) by which the qualities are known?... In empires and kingdoms the signs or signatures are titles... and the administrations attached to them. Explained.
What would the ordinations (in armies) be without ensigns, called standards?
Baptism is a sign in the Spiritual World.
The infant receives the sign of the cross... which is a sign of inauguration...
Like looking to Satan's sign instead of the sign of Christ.
The mark set on Cain an odour.
They elevated signs, and thus excited...
They stretch out the hand, which is a sign.
(A sign used for seeking out those who have done evil.) Described.
The signs of the conjunction of man with Heaven. Explained.
To stand for an ensign of the peoples () = to be seen by those in truths.
A man upon whom is the mark () = truth from good.
To set a sign among them () = to distinguish and separate from the evil, and conjoin with the good.
To give great signs and wonders = the efficacy and power of Falsities through confirmations from the sense of the letter, by which signs and prodigies are made in the Spiritual World.
Sail, and ensign () = manifestation; for spiritual truths are manifested through knowledges.

A sign = that which indicates, bears witness, and persuades concerning a matter in question; a miracle = that which excites, strikes with consternation, and induces amazement. Thus a sign moves the understanding, and a miracle the will. Illustrated.
That signs = testifications which indicate and persuade men to believe that a thing is so. Illustrated.
That a sign = testification about the certitude. Illustrated.
The ensigns placed upon the mountains, to gather together the people to war, etc. = indications to do the commandments. Illustrated. ( = convocation to the Church. AE 741:10.)
Signs = testifications and persuasions. AE 826. AE 1002.
They would have become profaners, and therefore He would not give them a sign.
Whatever the internal man produces, and presents to be seen and felt in the external, is called a sign (of charity). Explained.
By a sign is meant an indication and testification that it is so, because it marks and signifies, and indicates and testifies.
